name: יְרַחְמְאֵל
gloss: God has compassion; or may God have compassion
summary: Three men: Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron, of Judah, brother of Ram and Caleb, whose descendants the Jerahmeelites held cities in the Negeb (1Ch 2:9, 25–33, 42; 1Sa 27:10; 30:29); a Levite, son of Kish (1Ch 24:29); and Jerahmeel “son of the king”, sent by Jehoiakim to seize Baruch and Jeremiah, “but Yahweh hid them” (Jer 36:26). The name is the piel imperfect of רָחַם with אֵל: “God has compassion”, or as a wish, “may God have compassion”; scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “The sons of Hezron: יְרַחְמְאֵל, and Ram, and Chelubai.”
“The sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron.”
David's gifts “to those in the cities of the Jerahmeelite”.
“Of Kish: the sons of Kish, Jerahmeel.”
The king commanded “Jerahmeel the son of the king” to seize Baruch and Jeremiah, “but Yahweh hid them”.
“Yahweh will have compassion (יְרַחֵם) on Jacob”: the same verb form with the divine name as subject.

note: Takes t.bz.ak (the name, 8 tokens) and t.bz.al (the gentilic יְרַחְמְאֵלִי, 2 tokens), which TIPNR files under Jerahmeel@1Sa.27.10, the son of Hezron. “Son of the king” in Jer 36:26 may be a title of a royal official rather than Jehoiakim's son; TIPNR calls him son of Hammelech. Sabaean and Amorite names with rḥm and a god's name were not followed.
